questions.question: Which of the following is a group of primitive vertebrates having a large jawless sucking mouth, no limbs or paired fins and a completely cartilaginous skeleton with a persistent notochord?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclostomata.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Cyclostomata**

__
 
• a **group of vertebrates** that comprises the **living jawless fishes: the lampreys and hagfishes.**
 
• They are **modified and degenerate offshoots of the primitive vertebrate stalk.**
 
• Because of their **round mouths**, they are named Cyclostomata.
 
• Notochord persists **throughout life.**
 
• **The median fin is supported by cartilaginous fin-rays.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** ​Aschelminthes

 
• Closely associated with the **Platyhelminthes,** are an **obsolete phylum of pseudocoelomate **
 
• Commonly called r**oundworms,** the **body appears circular in the transverse cross-section.**
 
• They are **free-living or parasites**.
 
• They are found in **soil, freshwater, or as a parasite on plants, animals, and even humans.**
 
• The body is **bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic.**

**Hemichordata**

 
• Consist of three classes: **Enteropneusta, Pterobranchia, and Planctosphaeroidea**.
 
• Enteropneusts or acorn worms are **solitary, wormlike, bilaterally symmetrical animals, often brilliantly coloured**.
 
• They are known as acorn worms because of the **appearance of the proboscis and collar**.

**Arthropoda**

 
• **Invertebrate animals **have an **exoskeleton**, **a segmented body**, and **paired jointed appendages**.
 
• They form the** phylum Arthropoda**.
 
• They are distinguished by their** jointed limbs and cuticle made of chitin**, often **mineralised with calcium carbonate.**

questions.question: Which of the following characters are correct about Phylum Echinodermata?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coelom present, bilateral symmetry**__.

__
 
• **Echinodermata**

 
 
• Members of the phylum Echinodermata are commonly known as **Echinoderms**.
 
• Echinoderms are** marine organisms that live in both the intertidal zone and the ocean's depths**.
 
• **Characteristics of Echinodermata**
 
 
• They are** round or elongated and have a star-like appearance**.
 
• They are **exclusively marine** organisms.
 
• The organisms have **spiky skin**.
 
• **Organ system level organisation **can be seen in them. Most members have a **digestive system in addition to a circulatory system**.
 
• They have a **coelomic cavity and are triploblastic**.
 
• The body of an **adult echinoderm has radial symmetry**.
 
• **Larvae **of echinoderms show** bilateral symmetry**.

questions.question: What kind of adaptation is seen in bacteria when they form various kinds of thick-walled spores?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suspend**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Thick-Walled spore in Bacteria**

 
 
• In order to withstand **unfavourable conditions such intense boiling and freezing temperatures and ultraviolet radiations**, bacteria create** thick-walled spores **known as **endospores**.
 
• The organism may withstand **years of struggle inside such structures and germinate when the conditions are favourable**.

questions.question: The body of animals of the phylum Protozoa, such as Paramecium, Amoeba, Euglena, shows ________ grade organisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protoplasmic.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Protozoa is a phylum having **unicellular heterotrophs**. It comes under Kingdom Protista.
 
• A protozoan body consists of only a mass of protoplasm, so they are called acellular or non-cellular animals. Grade of organization: **protoplasmic grade of organization**.
 
• **Single-cell performs all the vital activities thus the single cell acts** like a whole body. The body** of protozoa is either naked or covered by a pellicle.**
 
• Protozoa can be divided into four phyla based on their locomotion: **Mastigophora, Sarcodina, Ciliophora, and Sporozoa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b1149550084fd4e895543d9f40fb390a035a2a2e0b6f723b3f1bed13d404409.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tissue-organ**_​ The organ level of organization is **when two or more tissues work together for a specific function**. For example, **the bladder consists of an inner lining of epithelial tissue, bound by various connective tissues to (smooth) muscle.**
 
• Most organisms have functional parts with five levels: **cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and whole organisms**.
 
• "Cellular organization" is **the defining property in living organisms.**

questions.question: Which phylum of the Kingdom Animalia includes animals such as Hydra, Adamsia, Physalia and Corals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coelenterata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coelenterata **is a term encompassing the animal **phyla Cnidaria **(**coral animals**, **true jellies**, **sea anemones**, **sea pens**, and **their relatives**) and **Ctenophora (comb jellies).**
 
• **They have **very **simple tissue organization**, with **only two layers of cells**, and **radial symmetry**.
 
• These are **mostly aquatic **or **marine habitat animals**.
 
• **The mouth **is **enclosed **by **thin **and **short tentacles**.
 
• **They have cavities **in **their body**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Platyhelminthes **or **platyhelminths **are a **phylum **of **relatively simple bilaterian**, **unsegmented**, soft**-bodied invertebrates**.
 
• **The annelids**, also known as **the ringed worms **or **segmented worms**, are **a large phylum**, with **over 22,000 extant **species **including ragworms**, **earthworms**, **and leeches**.
 
• **The members **of the **phylum Porifera**, are a **basal animal **clade as a **sister of the Diploblasts**. They are **multicellular organisms **that have **bodies full of pores **and **channels allowing water **to **circulate through **them, consisting of **jelly-like mesohyl sandwiched **between two **thin layers of cells**.

questions.question: How do the red algae reproduce vegetatively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Fragmentation.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red algae reproduce through ****Fragmentation**.

 
 
• **Red algae** is the numerous algae that **constitute the phylum Rhodophyta. **
 
• It contains a **red pigment** in addition to chlorophyll.
 
• The group includes **carrageen, dulse, and laver also called red seaweed.**
 
• It reproduces sexually as well as asexually.
 
• Asexual reproduction can occur through the production of spores and by vegetative means.
 
• It includes** fragmentation, cell division or propagules production.**
 
• **Fragmentation** is a method where **one fragment from an organism's body is broken due to external physical causes.**
 
• **Each fragment then grows into different individuals.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fission**

 
 
• **​**The type of asexual reproduction in which a **microorganism splits in two equal halves is called as binary fission.**
 
• **Binary fission occurs in Amoeba.**
 
• The cells which split during binary fission have the potential to grow to the size of the original one.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• ​**Spore formation **is a method of** asexual reproduction.**
 
• Plants like** ferns, moss, and fungi **reproduce by this method.
 
• **Spores are unicellular reproductive bodies** present in sacs called **sporangia.**
 
• When spores mature sporangia burst and spores are carried to a different location by air, wind, and water.
 
 
 
• **Cutting**
 
 
• **Cutting** is a type of asexual reproduction.
 
• **​**A cutting is a **vegetative plant part.**
 
• It is severed from the parent plant in order to regenerate itself, thereby forming a whole new plant.

questions.question: Which among the following pairs of 'animal - phylum of animal kingdom they belong' is incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Liver __**fluke - Nematoda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liver Fluke - 

 
 
• The scientific name of liver fluke is Fasciola hepatica.
 
• The life history of liver fluke involves two hosts (Digenetic parasitic).
 
• Primary host - Sheep and goat
 
• Secondary host - Garden snail (Planorbis, Lymnea)
 
• Liver fluke belongs to the **phylum Platyhelminthes, not Nematoda.**
 
• Liver fluke is a parasitic flatworm that infects the liver of its primary host, which is usually a sheep or goat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sycon - Porifera**

 
 
• Sycon is a sponge that belongs to the phylum Porifera.
 
• The common name of the Sycon is Crown Sponge.
 
• All sponges have a canal system that consists of the Ostia, spongocoel, and osculum.
 
• Canal system is one of the most important features of sponges.
 
• The canal system is a network of canals that connect the spongocoel to the outside via ostia.
 
• It helps in nutrition, respiration, and excretion processes.
 
 
 
• **Prawns - Arthropoda**
 
 
• Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (i.e.** a member of the order decapoda**), some of which can be eaten. 
 
• They belong to the kingdom Animalia and order **Arthropoda**.
 
 
 
• **​Starfish - Echinodermata**
 
 
• Starfish belongs to the phylum Echinodermata group.
 
• Echinodermata are so named owing to their spiny skin (from the Greek “echinos” meaning “spiny” and “dermos” meaning “skin”).
 
• Echinodermata are exclusively marine organisms. Sea stars, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, sand dollars, and brittle stars are all examples of echinoderms.

questions.question: Which group of animals has a body wall composed of both circular and longitudinal muscle fibres surrounded by a moist, cellular cuticle that is secreted by an epidermal epithelium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Annelida.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Besides being segmented, the body wall of Annelida is characterized by being made up of both circular and longitudinal muscle fibres surrounded by a moist, acellular cuticle that is secreted by an epidermal epithelium.
 
• The body cavity of annelids is lined by epithelium.
 
• Successive body segments are separated by walls that correspond to the external rings. 
 
• In grooves between the segments of some oligochaetes are dorsal pores through which coelomic fluid may be discharged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phylum Arthropoda **contains a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.**
 
• The flatworms, flatworms, Platyhelminthes, or platyhelminths are a phylum of relatively simple bilaterian, unsegmented, soft-bodied invertebrates.
 
• Coelenterata is **a term encompassing the animal phyla Cnidaria (coral animals, true jellies, sea anemones, sea pens, and their relatives) and Ctenophora (comb jellies)**.

questions.question: Locomotion in ______ takes place with the help of a muscular foot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snails.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The snail is a very **slow-moving animal.**
 
• Like an **earthworm**, a snail too has a** liquid skeleton.**
 
• Snails have a** shell**, inside which they can hide to protect themselves from the heat of the sun and enemies.
 
• The shell is the **outer skeleton**, but it is **not made of bones**.
 
• For movement, **a thick structure and the head of the snail **come out of an opening in the shell.
 
• The thick structure is its** foot**, made of** strong muscles.**
 
• The** muscular foot produces wave-like movements** that push the **snail’s body forward.**
 
• A **trail of mucous** is left behind when the snail crawls.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Jellyfish**
 Jellyfish are animals of the phylum Cnidaria. They have no brain, heart, bones or eyes. They are made up of a smooth, bag-like body and tentacles armed with tiny, stinging cells.
 
 

 **Sea urchins**
 Sea urchins are the Class Echinoidea of the Phylum Echinodermata. These creatures are typically small, spiny, and round. They live in all the earth’s oceans, at depths ranging from the tide line to 15,000 feet.
 
 

 **Earthworms**
 Earthworms are classified in the phylum Annelida or Annelids. They are the main contributors to enriching and improving soil for plants, animals and even humans.
